notes: This source/test traceability contract covers only the bounded IEEE 1516.1-2025 regional interaction declaration and no-time Send Interaction With Regions slice in Umbra's opt-in, non-installable development profile. It validates owner-created committed region specifications, available-dimension context, independent regional subscription state, per-(interaction-class, region) active/passive state, strict 2025 region-set overlap, callback-entry rechecks, and the empty-region no-op rules. The focused service-report case now also proves the accepted §9.10 and §9.11 transitions append recipient-local successful-void records with type-27 InteractionClassHandle, type-43 RegionHandleSet, and the type-6 passive-indicator Boolean before the next interaction operation; paired C++ cases cover both the configured filesystem and HLA_IMMEDIATE MOM routes, including passive-indicator inversion and stable serial order. A paired ordinary Send Interaction With Regions failure matrix now records invalid interaction-class, parameter, and region inputs through both the configured filesystem and HLA_IMMEDIATE MOM routes with type-27/type-40/type-43/type-63/type-34 forms, false indicators, Null returns, exact exceptions, and no application callback. The dedicated Allow Relaxed DDM regression adds a direct-source, implementation-specific exact-boundary expansion while preserving strict overlap; RL-030 records the lack of an immutable Lab candidate for §9.1.4/§9.1.8 policy prose. Passive pairs remain subscribed and retain their region-use fence, but cannot arrange delivery; a later subscription of the same pair changes its mode. The passive-subscription definition supplies the delivery predicate, while the Lab's immutable candidate records cover the service's active/passive pair-state language. Object-instance regional registration/association, object-class attribute regional subscriptions, Request Attribute Value Update With Regions, timestamped/retraction behavior, realization/association state, broader relaxed-DDM matrices, save/restore, remote transport, package support, catalog evidence, and conformance remain outside this slice. The contract uses immutable candidate IDs exported by the Requirements Lab, including its current source-title path mismatch.
